sheet-1.description: Sheet 1 covers the northern edge of Bloomfield, along the Passaic County line, and is drawn at 200 feet to an inch. It is almost entirely open country: large farm tracts and estates, each lettered with its owner's name, with a few scattered frame dwellings and farm buildings coloured yellow. Broad Street runs from the top left of the sheet southeast and then south down the west side, bending east at the bottom to follow the Third River valley toward the Morris Canal. Alexander Avenue, which changes its name to Mt. Heborn Road where it crosses the Volume Three match line, meets Broad Street near the top left. Bellevue Avenue branches south-west from Broad Street near the foot of the sheet, and West Passaic Avenue leaves Broad Street at the lower right corner. A broad strip marked as the East Jersey Water Co right of way, carrying the Newark City pipe lines, crosses the sheet from upper left to lower right. The Third River winds through the centre of the sheet and Pearl Brook flows beside the bottom edge. The Morris Canal runs down the right side of the sheet as a wide blue band. The left margin carries a dash-dot match line and the note See Volume Three; a dash-dot line at the top marks the Passaic County boundary. A compass rose with a north arrow stands at the top right, turned about 30 degrees from the page vertical. Neighbouring sheets 2 and 3 are indicated in the margins.
notes: Alexander Avenue and Mt. Heborn Road: the modern street is Alexander Avenue; Mount Hebron Road is a separate modern street not joined to Broad Street in the street data.
Broad Street at the foot of the sheet is lettered only 'Broad' with no suffix.
Bellevue Avenue / Broad Street: the junction as drawn lies about 20 to 30 m from the modern node and was left out of the control.
The Garden State Parkway now crosses the sheet diagonally through the farm tracts, from upper left to lower right.

200 ft, turned about -33. Farmland along Broad St, Alexander Av and Bellevue Av near the Passaic County line; Morris Canal. Helmert from one junction plus two corners carried from sheet 2. Bellevue/Broad and Broad/West Passaic modern nodes 20-26 m off the drawn junctions (left out).

sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 lies in the north-eastern corner of Bloomfield along the Passaic County line, at 200 feet to an inch. It is mostly open farmland divided into long tracts lettered with their owners' names (Elizabeth Baldwin Est., C. E. W. Harvey, Peter Garrabrant, Arthur Russell, E. Van Winkle, Campbell Bros, Ellen Simonson and others), with only a few scattered frame dwellings and farm buildings along the roads. The Morris Canal runs down the left edge as a wide blue band, with the Third River crossing the lower left corner. Broad Street leaves the lower left corner northward and meets West Passaic Avenue, which runs north-east across the farms; Briar Avenue runs north from West Passaic Avenue toward the county line. East Passaic Avenue runs south from the middle of the sheet and then north-east and north to the top right corner. Day Street links West and East Passaic Avenues across the Arthur Russell tract. A strip of the East Jersey Water Co right of way, with the Newark City pipe lines, crosses the sheet from upper left to lower right. Along the right edge, beside the Nutley boundary, Joerg Avenue is lined by short cross streets (Kingsland Road, Charles Street, Cadmus Street and High Street) laid out in unbuilt blocks, with one small pond near Kingsland Road. The only public building is the Brookdale Public School No. 3, a brick school on Broad Street at the lower left. The right margin reads Town of Nutley and See Volume One, and the Passaic County line is a dash-dot line across the top. A compass rose near the top is turned about 33 degrees from the page vertical.
notes: Briar Avenue north of West Passaic Avenue is not a modern street in the extract (Briar Lane is a different street).
The drawn Passaic Avenue junctions north-east of Day Street do not match the modern West Passaic Avenue nodes and were not used as control.
Kingsland Road is now Kingsland Street.
Brookdale Public School No. 3 stands on Broad Street at the lower left.
200 ft, turned about -33. Farmland; West and East Passaic Av, Day St, Briar Av, Joerg Av at the Nutley line. 4 points.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 covers the western edge of Bloomfield, along the Montclair boundary, at 200 feet to an inch. It is farmland and large estates, the owners' names (John Hyde, A. Garrabrant, Tunis Garrabrant, A. Yereance, W. M. Brocaw, Michael Armbruster, M. L. Davidson, J. B. Bray) lettered across long narrow tracts, with detached frame houses and farm buildings strung along the roads. Broad Street enters at the top, runs east along the north side of the sheet and then turns south down the east side; Bellevue Avenue branches off at the top left and runs west to the Montclair line. Near the top right Broad Street meets the road to West Passaic Avenue, with the Morris Canal and the Third River crossing the corner. Watchung Avenue leaves Broad Street near the bottom right and runs south-west to the Glen Ridge boundary, where it meets Ridgewood Avenue at the lower left, with a 16 inch water pipe along it. The Brookdale Reformed Church, its chapel and a cemetery stand on Bellevue Avenue at the top left, and the Brookdale Baptist Church is on the north side of Broad Street. The left margin shows the dash-dot Montclair town line, a strip of Glen Ridge Borough at the bottom left and the note See Volume Three. A compass rose near the lower right is turned about 33 degrees from the page vertical. Adjoining sheets are numbered 1, 2, 4 and 5 in the margins.
notes: The junction of Bellevue Avenue and Broad Street is drawn about 20 m from the modern node; it was not used as control.
The modern node Broad Street / West Passaic Avenue lies about 26 m south of the drawn junction of the north-west leg of Broad Street with the road to West Passaic Avenue.
Brookdale Reformed Church and Brookdale Baptist Church are lettered on the sheet.
200 ft, turned about -34. Broad St, Bellevue Av, Watchung Av, Ridgewood Av on the Montclair line; 2 junctions plus 2 corners carried from sheet 2.

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 shows the Bay Avenue and Myrtle Avenue district of north-western Bloomfield, drawn at 200 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. Bay Avenue, with Franklin Avenue as its southward continuation, runs down the left side of the sheet, carrying a 4 inch water pipe, and Broad Street crosses the top edge. Myrtle Avenue runs across the middle of the sheet from the left edge toward the lower right, crossed by Morris Avenue, Birch Street and, at the right, Herbert Street. Between Bay Avenue and Morris Avenue a small grid of platted but largely unbuilt streets (Mill Street, Lakewood Terrace, Augusta Street, Chapel Street and Pulaski Street) is laid out in empty blocks. East of Morris Avenue the land is divided into long farm tracts (W. A. Baldwin, John Cockefair, P. N. Jackson, Wm Fritz, J. D. Lerry Est., John J. Florus, Philip Glaab, S. Cockefair), with a few houses and the S. Cockefair farm buildings in the upper right corner. Two streams cross the upper part of the sheet and feed ponds near Broad Street. The Morris Canal curves along the lower edge beside East Passaic Avenue, here also lettered Canal Street, which forms the boundary with the Town of Nutley; the area below is left blank with the note See Volume One. Small groups of dwellings stand on Franklin Avenue and East Passaic Avenue at the lower left. Two fire alarm boxes are marked near the left edge. A compass rose with a north arrow stands at the lower right. Neighbouring sheets 4, 6, 8 and 10 are numbered in the margins.
notes: East Passaic Avenue at the bottom is lettered 'E. Passaic Av. or Canal St.'.
Myrtle Avenue is now Broughton Avenue; Morris Avenue (north-south) is now Pettit Street; Augusta Street is now Augustus Street; Franklin Avenue is now Hoover Avenue.
Mill Street / Augustus Street: the modern node lies about 11 m from the drawn junction and was rejected from the fit.
Parcels were not used for the fit (leave-one-out improved from 5.3 m to 3.7 m without them).
200 ft, turned +67. Bay Av, Myrtle Av (= Broughton Avenue), Morris Av (= Pettit Street), Augusta St (= Augustus Street), Mill St grid, Morris Canal. 9 points, use_parcels false.

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 covers the north-eastern edge of Bloomfield beside the Nutley line, at 200 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. Broad Street crosses the top of the sheet; Watchung Avenue leaves it near the top and runs south-east and then south, following the Morris Canal, to East Passaic Avenue near the foot of the sheet. Myrtle Avenue crosses the left half of the sheet and meets Herbert Street at the left edge. Most of the sheet is farmland and marsh in long tracts lettered with their owners' names (A. Walker, Alex Parsons, S. B. Stimus, P. and H. Gehring, Jas. Payne, Jas. Gilman, J. Zimmerer, Laycock, Martin Hummel, John Van Riper and Wilbur Brocaw), with a few dwellings and farm buildings, a wood chopping shop and a blacksmith near Broad Street, and the Bloomfield Poor House near Watchung Avenue. The Third River winds across the middle of the sheet through an area marked Marsh Land, and the Morris Canal crosses diagonally below it. At the lower left, below East Passaic Avenue or Canal Street, an unbuilt grid of the Town of Nutley (Mount Vernon, Thomas or Clement, Center, Ridge and Van Winkle) is drawn in outline, and the Nutley town line, a dash-dot line, runs across the foot of the sheet. A few houses stand at the lower right around Davis Avenue, Chappel Lane and Payne Street, with the East Jersey Water Co right of way and Newark City pipe lines in the corner. The foot of the sheet carries the note See Volume One and a compass rose with a north arrow.
notes: East Passaic Avenue at the lower left is lettered 'E. Passaic Av. or Canal St.'; the Nutley street lettered 'Thomas St. or Clement Av.' has two names.
Myrtle Avenue is now Broughton Avenue.
The drawn Nutley grid (Mount Vernon, Thomas or Clement, Center, Van Winkle) did not match the modern street nodes within about 55 m and was not used as control.
The south leg of Watchung Avenue along the Morris Canal no longer exists; the modern Watchung Avenue runs straight south-east from Broad Street.
200 ft, turned +67. Broad St, Watchung Av, Myrtle Av; Nutley grid in outline (displaced about 55 m against modern streets, not used). Helmert from one junction plus two corners carried from sheet 5.

sheet-7.description: Sheet 7 shows the northern edge of Bloomfield along the Glen Ridge border, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the top. The map is mostly open land with only scattered frame dwellings. Broad Street runs from the top of the sheet down the middle and bends south past the Third River, which winds beside it from Bay Avenue to the bottom edge. Bay Avenue crosses the upper part from west to east and then turns southeast, where Franklin Avenue branches from it and returns southwest to Broad Street. Morris Avenue runs between Bay and Franklin Avenues through a wedge of large unbuilt tracts, with Lakewood Terrace, Mill Street and Myrtle Avenue entering Bay Avenue from the north. Essex Avenue forms the west side of the sheet; a dash-dot line along it marks the boundary of Glen Ridge Borough. Warren Street crosses the lower third between Essex Avenue and Broad Street, and below it a row of narrow lots with small dwellings fronts Baldwin Street along the bottom, with a pond and a branch of the river near Franklin Avenue. Water mains of 4, 6 and 12 inches are marked in Bay Avenue, Broad Street, Warren Street and Baldwin Street, and there are fire alarm boxes at Broad Street and Bay Avenue and at the east end of Bay Avenue. The scale bar and a compass rose are at the lower right. The neighbouring sheets are numbered in the margins: 4 and 5 above, 8 to the northeast, 10 to the east, 12 to the west, 9 below Franklin Avenue and 16 below Baldwin Street.
notes: Franklin Avenue is today's Hoover Avenue.
Morris Avenue and Myrtle Avenue as drawn here are not in the modern street network, and were not used as control.
100 ft. Glen Ridge line along Essex Av; Broad St, Bay Av, Franklin Av (= Hoover Avenue), Morris Av (= Morris Place), Third River.

sheet-8.description: Sheet 8 covers the northern part of Bloomfield between Bay Avenue and the Morris Canal, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. The sheet is turned on the page, and the compass rose at the lower right shows north pointing toward the upper right. Bay Avenue runs down the left side from Morris Avenue at the upper left to Franklin Avenue at the lower left. Mill Street and Myrtle Avenue cross the sheet from Bay Avenue toward the east, and Lakewood Terrace runs along the top. Augusta Street, Chapel Street and Pulaski Street are the cross streets of a small built-up district in the middle, where narrow lots on Mill Street, Lakewood Terrace and Myrtle Avenue hold detached frame dwellings, with a few stables and outbuildings. One building near the middle of the Mill Street block is coloured green, and the Broughton Memorial Chapel of the Presbyterian church stands on Myrtle Avenue near Bay Avenue, with its heating and lighting noted. A saw mill stands on a brook at the upper right, where a stream also crosses the top of the sheet. The lower half is largely open land, divided into large unbuilt tracts, with Morris Avenue along the right side. Franklin Avenue descends from Bay Avenue to the Morris Canal at the bottom, where it crosses on a bridge and meets Plane Street and East Passaic Avenue on the far bank. A few dwellings and a row of small buildings lie along the canal. A boundary line of the Town of Nutley appears at the lower right, with a note to see Volume One. Water mains are marked in Bay Avenue, Mill Street and Franklin Avenue, and the scale bar is at the lower left. Neighbouring sheets are numbered 5, 6, 7, 9 and 10 in the margins.
notes: Myrtle Avenue is today's Broughton Avenue (the Broughton Memorial Chapel stands on it); Franklin Avenue is today's Hoover Avenue; Augusta Street is today's Augustus Street.
The Morris Avenue at the upper left is today's Morris Place. The Morris Avenue along the right edge is not in the modern street network.
The vertical street at the right end of the Pulaski Street block, also lettered Pulaski Street, is probably today's Howard Street and was not used as control.
The Combination Rubber Mfg Co works is not drawn on this sheet.
100 ft, turned about 49. Bay Av, Mill St, Myrtle Av (= Broughton Avenue), Augusta St (= Augustus Street), Chapel, Pulaski, Franklin Av (= Hoover Avenue); Morris Canal. Martin St left out (27 m).

sheet-9-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 9 is the main map of an industrial district in northern Bloomfield, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the top. Broad Street runs down the left side of the sheet, widening where Warren Street comes in from the west and curving southward past Baldwin Street to James Street at the bottom edge. Franklin Avenue crosses the top of the sheet from Broad Street toward the northeast, with a row of four frame houses numbered 392 to 398. East of Broad Street the Third River winds south through the middle of the sheet, and beyond it the Morris Canal and a parallel road cross the sheet diagonally from the northeast. The dominant feature is the Diamond Mills Paper Co. (D. W. Thompson, president), a large brick and frame mill on the Third River fed by a head race and iron flume, with machine shop, finishing, rotary, stock, crimping and store rooms, a pump room and a 550 horsepower engine; a long note at the right describes its watchman service, sprinklers and fire pump. Along the east side of Broad Street between Baldwin and James Streets stand a meat market, dwellings, a barber shop and the Excelsior Hose Co. No. 3 volunteer fire house. Baldwin Street crosses the river on a bridge. Much of the west side of Broad Street is left blank because it is drawn on sheets 7 and 16. The lower right corner of the sheet, behind a heavy line, is a separate inset (part 2) showing the Combination Rubber Mfg. Co.
notes: Franklin Avenue on this sheet is today's Hoover Avenue (it meets Broad Street at the modern Broad Street / Hoover Avenue junction).
The Morris Canal bed is now the Garden State Parkway; the canal-side road and the mill site have no modern street junctions.
Placed from junctions along Broad Street and four parcel block corners at Baldwin and Warren Streets; the east half of the part is extrapolated.

Broad St, Franklin Av (= Hoover Avenue), Warren St, Baldwin, James; Diamond Mills Paper Co on Third River; Morris Canal (now Garden State Parkway). 50 ft. Two parts: part 1 main map; part 2 inset at lower right behind a heavy line: Combination Rubber Mfg Co on the other Franklin Av by the Morris Canal (no surviving junction).

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Combination Rubber Mfg Co on Franklin Av by the Morris Canal (no surviving street junction (area now Garden State Parkway); needs carried points from sheet-10 (the works is drawn there at 200 ft, upper left); the building outline differs in length between the two drawings (about 134 against 160 ft)).

sheet-10.description: Sheet 10 is an outlying sheet of northern Bloomfield drawn at 200 feet to an inch with north toward the top, mostly open land and water. Franklin Avenue crosses the top from the Morris Canal at the upper left to the Nutley line at the upper right, with the large unbuilt tract of the Glen Ridge Cemetery beside it. At the upper left the Morris Canal runs southwest past Plane Street, where a few frame dwellings and St. Valentines R.C. Church with its school and parsonage stand on a long narrow block, and past the works of the Combination Rubber Mfg Co., which is drawn in outline and referred to sheet 9. In the middle the Third River winds through Davey's Pond and returns toward Oakes Pond at the lower left; at the Third River on the right the E. H. Davey Co. premises are marked with a reference to sheet 63. At the lower left the works of Thos. Oakes & Co. stand by Oakes Pond, shown as a group of pink brick buildings with a reference to sheet 20, and the Morris Canal runs down the left edge. A small settlement lies along James Street and Spring Street, beside the Mt. Olive R.C. Cemetery, which fills a block bounded by Barth Street. Bellville Avenue runs along the bottom with a few streets leaving it: Spruce, Walnut, Williamson, Clarendon, Orchard, Smith and Morton; Davey Street and Davey Lane run diagonally through the right half. A strip along the right edge is blank, with the notes Township of Belleville and See Volume One. Neighbouring sheets are numbered 5, 7, 8, 16, 18, 19, 52, 53, 55 and 56 in the margins. A compass rose and the scale note are at the right.
notes: Franklin Avenue is today's Hoover Avenue; Bellville Avenue is today's Belleville Avenue; Plane Street is part of today's North Spring Street (probable, from the fit).
The Combination Rubber Mfg Co. is drawn at the upper left and E. H. Davey Co. at the middle right; each refers to another sheet (9 and 63) where it is drawn in more detail.
Drawn at 200 feet to an inch.
East Passaic Avenue at Franklin Avenue was rejected as a control point (11.6 m from the fit).

200 ft. Morris Canal, Third River, Davey's Pond, Oakes Pond; Combination Rubber Mfg Co (upper left, see sheet 9) and E. H. Davey Co (see sheet 63); Bellville Av along the bottom; Plane St (= part of North Spring Street, inferred).

sheet-16.description: Sheet 16 shows a residential district in the north of Bloomfield on the Glen Ridge line, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the right. Essex Avenue runs along the top of the sheet, with a dash-dot borough boundary along it, and Broad Street crosses the lower part on a long diagonal that bends east at James Street. Four streets run down the page from Essex Avenue toward Broad Street: Osborne Street on the left, then William Street, Pitt Street, and Baldwin Street along the right edge. The blocks between them are lined with detached frame dwellings on deep narrow lots, with stables and outbuildings, mostly one to two and a half storeys. The large block between Pitt and Baldwin Streets holds the Brookside Public School, a pink brick building with an open assembly hall and an annex, with notes on heating, lighting and hose. Near Broad Street the buildings become more commercial: a hotel with sheds being built, a cement block construction works, a bakery, groceries, a cobbler, a pool room and a club house, and near the lower left a clubhouse and curb office. A cement block works of Delp and Shuboy stands at the bottom near the Morris Canal, which crosses the lower left corner. Water mains of 6 and 12 inches are marked in Essex Avenue, Broad Street and the cross streets, and a compass rose with a north arrow is at the right. Neighbouring sheets are numbered in the margins: 15 above Essex Avenue, 17 and 18 to the west, 7 to the east, 9 and 10 below.
notes: Osborne, Pitt, Baldwin, Broad and James are today's Osborne Street, Pitt Street, Baldwin Street, Broad Street and James Street; no modern William Street was found near this sheet and it was not used as control.
Essex Avenue is drawn only to its south edge, so its centreline points were placed half the labelled 66 feet beyond the block edge (hand-picked).
50 ft, north right. Essex Av to Broad St, Osborne, William (gone), Pitt, Baldwin; Brookside Public School. Two boundary junctions hand-picked.

sheet-18.description: Sheet 18 covers a residential strip of northern Bloomfield between Broad Street and the Morris Canal, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the right. Broad Street crosses the top of the sheet on a long diagonal from the upper left to the right edge. Maple Street runs down the left side of the sheet, Almira runs down the middle from Broad Street toward the canal, and Benson Street and Osborne Street enter Broad Street from the right. Spruce Street meets Maple Street at the lower left. At the upper left the Erie R.R. Greenwood Lake Division crosses Broad Street and Maple Street on a diagonal, with water mains of 4, 6 and 12 inches and a fire alarm box beside it. The blocks between Maple Street and Almira, and east of Almira, are laid out in narrow lots with detached frame dwellings of two or two and a half storeys, a few stables and sheds, and a coloured cooper's shop; the lots at the upper end of the Maple Street block are deeper. The only industrial premises is Robt. E. Day's cement block making works in the upper middle, with a storage building for cement blocks. The east side of Almira ends in a large undivided tract with a few outbuildings, while a strip of lots along the right edge belongs to the neighbouring sheet. The Morris Canal curves across the lower half with its towpath, and Oakes Pond and a branch of the Third River lie below it. A compass rose with a north arrow is at the top and the scale of feet at the lower right. Neighbouring sheets are numbered in the margins: 17 above Broad Street, 19 to the west, 16 to the east and 10 below the canal.
notes: Maple, Almira, Benson Street and Osborne Street are today's Maple Street, Almira Street, Benson Street and Osborne Street.
Four of the five control points lie along Broad Street, so the placement rests on one street plus the Maple and Spruce junction; the leave-one-out figure is not meaningful.
50 ft, north right. Broad St, Maple, Almira; Morris Canal; Robt. E. Day cement block works. Four of five points on Broad Street (low).

sheet-19.description: Sheet 19 shows a residential district of northern Bloomfield between Belleville Avenue and Maple Street, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the right. Broad Street curves across the top of the sheet, and a dashed line along it marks a boundary. Spruce runs along the bottom. Belleville Avenue runs down the left side, New runs down the middle from Broad Street to Spruce, and Maple runs down the right side; State Street enters Broad Street from the top right, and Elm Street and Oak Street are short stubs entering Belleville Avenue from the left edge. The Erie R.R. Greenwood Lake Division crosses the whole sheet on a broad diagonal from the lower left to the upper right, with several tracks, and divides the district into two parts. Frame dwellings of two or two and a half storeys stand on large lots with stables and coops west of New Street, and on narrower lots along New Street and Maple Street, where the dwellings are close together. The one industrial property is the Bloomfield Coal and Supply Co. beside the railroad near the upper right, with a long wood shed and high coal pockets served by sidings, an office and scales. A park is lettered across a large tract at the top near Broad Street. Water mains of 4, 6 and 12 inches are marked in the streets, with fire alarm boxes near the corners at the upper right and lower left. The scale of feet is at the bottom right, and a compass rose with its north arrow is at the lower left. Neighbouring sheets are numbered in the margins: 17 above Broad Street, 48 to the west, 18 to the east and 20 below Spruce.
notes: The streets are today's Broad Street, Belleville Avenue, New Street, Maple Street, Spruce Street, State Street, Elm Street and Oak Street.
The Erie R.R. Greenwood Lake Division is abandoned; its line is not used as control.
Printed name 'Park' lies on a large tract beside Broad Street; it is not a street.
50 ft, north right. Broad, Belleville Av, New, Maple, Spruce; Erie Greenwood Lake Division; Bloomfield Coal & Supply Co.

sheet-23.description: Sheet 23 shows a mostly open district of large lots north of the centre of Bloomfield, drawn at 50 feet to the inch and turned so that north lies to the right of the page. Edgewood Road runs along the top, where the line between the Borough of Glen Ridge and the Town of Bloomfield is drawn, and Park Av. runs down the left side. State crosses the middle of the sheet from Park Av. to Belleville Av. on the right, and Broad crosses near the bottom, running on to the right. Jersey St. enters from the left near Park Av. and Beach St. leaves Broad at the lower left. The blocks between Edgewood Road and State hold a few detached frame dwellings and outbuildings, with several wide parcels of land lacking buildings. A rectangular block bounded by State and Broad holds a storage building and an open shed, and a larger house stands on a block near Broad. The area is thinly built up, and most of the sheet shows only lot lines, street lines and water mains. The mains are lettered in the street centres: a pair of mains of 12 and 6 inches in Broad. A fire alarm box stands at the corner of Park Av. and State. The neighbouring sheets are 22 above, 26 and 24 on the left, 17 and 48 on the right and below.
notes: Streets keep their present names; the printed Park Av. is Park Avenue today.
The sheet is turned about 66 degrees from north-up; seven junctions were detected automatically.
50 ft, turned. Edgewood Road, Park Av, State, Belleville Av, Broad, Jersey St; open lots.

sheet-26.description: Sheet 26 covers a residential district north of the centre of Bloomfield, bounded on the south by Liberty and on the north by Park Av. Bloomfield Av. runs diagonally down the left side, and State runs down the right side. Jersey crosses the upper middle between Park Av. and the street called Park, which runs across the middle of the sheet to meet State. Clark St. leaves Bloomfield Av. toward the west near the bottom left. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to the inch with north at the top. Most of the buildings are frame dwellings with porches, set in large lots, with a few outbuildings. Christ Church Episcopal and its parish house stand at the upper left corner on Bloomfield Av., with a rectory beside them, and the Glen Ridge borough and Bloomfield town line follows the avenue there. Along Bloomfield Av. south of the middle are the Bloomfield Hotel with a bowling alley, a lyceum and other buildings. A church with a school hall stands near State at the lower right, and a number of small dwellings are packed along the lower end of Bloomfield Av. and State. Water pipes are drawn in the street centres and fire alarm boxes stand at the Park Av. and State corner and at Liberty. The neighbouring sheets are 22, 23, 24, 25, 27 and 28.
notes: Park Av. is Park Avenue today and the street printed Park is Park Street; Edgewood Rd. is Edgewood Road.
The modern Bloomfield Avenue and Hillside Avenue junction is drawn about 10 m from the modern node and is excluded.
50 ft. Park Av, Park, Jersey, State, Bloomfield Av, Clark St, Edgewood Road; residential. Bloomfield/Hillside excluded.

sheet-27.description: Sheet 27 lies on the Glen Ridge and Bloomfield town line west of the centre of Bloomfield and is drawn at 50 feet to the inch with north tilted slightly to the right of the page top. Clark crosses the top of the sheet, Thomas runs down the left side, and Farrand runs down the right side from Clark to Washington Av. at the bottom, where Winsor Pl. leaves Thomas toward the left. Bloomfield Av. is seen in the upper right corner. The Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Montclair branch railroad runs through the middle of the sheet, and Toney's Brook crosses it, winding from Clark to Washington Av. The principal industry is the Consolidated Safety Pin Co. Inc., whose long group of brick buildings stands between the brook and Farrand, with a lettered description of its fire protection in the upper left. Other works include a foundry, a japanning building and a store house. Along the east side of Farrand are rows of dwellings and shops, and People's Ice Co. stands near the railroad at the bottom. The streets on the west side, between Thomas and the brook, hold dwellings on narrow lots. Lines on the sheet mark the boundary between the Borough of Glen Ridge and the Town of Bloomfield, which crosses diagonally from lower left to upper right. Neighbouring sheets are numbered 25, 26, 28, 31, 32 and 41.
notes: Thomas Street, Clark Street, Farrand Street and Ward Street keep these names; the printed Washington Av. is Washington Street today.
Control rests on three detected junctions and one hand-picked one at the left edge (Thomas and Washington); treat placement as low to medium confidence.
The modern Farrand Street curves west near Washington Street and does not follow the drawn line there; that junction was not used.
50 ft. Consolidated Safety Pin Co, Toney's Brook, D.L.&W. Montclair Branch; Clark, Thomas, Farrand, Ward St, Washington Av. 4 points (low-medium).

sheet-28.description: Sheet 28 shows the centre of Bloomfield where Bloomfield Avenue, the main street of the town, runs diagonally from the upper left to the lower right. Liberty crosses the top of the sheet from Bloomfield Avenue eastward to Broad, with State Street entering from the north and ending at Liberty. Ward runs from Bloomfield Avenue to the lower left to meet Farrand, which crosses the west side of the sheet, and Washington Av. closes the sheet at the bottom, where Glenwood Av. continues Bloomfield Avenue toward the south east. Broad runs down the right side, with Franklin St. leaving it at the upper right. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to the inch with north at the top. The area is mixed commercial and industrial. On the west side are the Jenkins Mfg. Co. plant, a wagon and horse shoeing shop of M. S. Palmer, a Torbensen motor car company works, the Central Fire House, and a livery stable of T. H. Decker. A row of stores, a laundry, a bakery, a post office, a bank with a rounded corner and other shops lines the east side of Bloomfield Avenue and Broad. A paint and oil dealer and a hay and grain store stand near Washington Av. The Glen Ridge borough and Bloomfield town line is shown in the upper left corner. Fire alarm boxes are marked at several corners.
notes: Bloomfield Avenue, Liberty Street, Broad Street, Ward Street, State Street and Farrand Street keep these names; the printed Washington Av. is Washington Street today.
The modern Farrand Street and the Washington Street and Bloomfield Avenue junction are displaced from the drawn lines by 30 m or more and were not used for control.
Only four junctions could be measured; the Bloomfield Avenue and Liberty junction lies in a wide fan of street lines and was not detected.

50 ft. Centre of Bloomfield: Bloomfield Av, Broad, Liberty, State, Franklin, Ward, Farrand, Washington Av, Glenwood Av. Washington Street left out (modern nodes about 30 m off the drawn junctions). 4 points.

sheet-37.description: Sheet 37 covers a residential district on the line between the Borough of Glen Ridge and the Town of Bloomfield, drawn at 50 feet to the inch and turned so that north lies to the right of the page. Midland Avenue bounds the sheet at the top, with Maolis Avenue on the left and Linden Avenue on the right running down the page. Ashland Avenue crosses the middle of the sheet between Maolis and Linden Avenues, and Clinton crosses near the bottom, where the street lines converge toward the lower left. The blocks between Midland and Ashland Avenues hold a row of small frame dwellings with outbuildings and two larger buildings, one of them a wide structure near the Linden Avenue end. South of Ashland Avenue the blocks are only partly built up, with a handful of dwellings and sheds scattered along the lot lines; the lower part of the sheet, down to Clinton, is largely open land cut into lots. The borough and town boundary is drawn as a dash-dot line crossing the upper blocks. Water mains are shown in the middle of the street lines, with their sizes lettered along them. Fire alarm boxes stand at the Maolis and Midland corner and at the Linden and Ashland corner. The neighbouring sheets are numbered in the margins: 34 above, 38 to the right, 43 to the left and 39 below.
notes: Streets keep their names today: Midland Avenue, Ashland Avenue, Linden Avenue, Maolis Avenue and Clinton Street.
Georeferenced from six street junctions located where the printed water mains cross; the sheet is turned about 69 degrees from north-up.
50 ft, north right. Midland Av, Ashland Av, Linden Av, Maolis Av, Clinton.

sheet-38-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 38 is the main map, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the right. It covers a residential district on the line between the Borough of Glen Ridge and the Town of Bloomfield, whose boundary runs as a dash-dot line across the middle of the upper block. Midland Avenue runs across the top of the sheet and Ashland Avenue across the middle, both meeting Washington Avenue at the right, where Washington Place comes in from the east. Linden Avenue runs down the left side and meets Clinton Street, which crosses the lower part of the sheet diagonally toward Washington Avenue. The two long blocks between Midland and Ashland Avenues and between Ashland Avenue and Clinton Street are lined with detached frame dwellings on deep lots, with stables at the rear; a few houses toward Clinton Street are marked as flats. There are no factories or institutions on this part; the only coloured buildings besides dwellings are two small outbuildings near Washington Avenue. Water mains and a fire alarm box are marked at Linden Avenue. Adjoining sheets are numbered in the margins: 34 above Midland Avenue, 37 to the west, 31 to the east and 40 below Clinton Street. The bottom of the sheet is taken up by two insets behind heavy lines (parts 2 and 3), which show industrial premises in the Watsessing district at a larger scale than sheet 44.
notes: Washington Avenue on this part is today's Washington Street (south of Douglas Road).
Clinton is today's Clinton Street.

Midland Av, Ashland Av, Linden Av, Clinton, Washington Av (= Washington Street); Glen Ridge / Bloomfield line. 50 ft, north to the right. Three parts: 1 main; 2 inset (lower centre) Ellor Bros & Hall hat works at Westcott/Thornton/Prospect; 3 inset (lower right) The Nitram Co on Peloubet / E. Maolis Av / Orange. Both insets enlarge areas of sheet 44.

sheet-38-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 38 is an inset at the lower centre of the sheet, behind a heavy line, showing the works of Ellor Bros. & Hall (Sam. Ellor, manager), makers of soft hats, in the Watsessing district of Bloomfield at the East Orange line. The inset is drawn at 50 feet to an inch, twice the scale of sheet 44, where the same premises appear in the block at Westcott and Thornton Streets; its north arrow points roughly to the right. Westcott Street runs across the top of the inset and ends at Thornton Street, which runs down the right side to Prospect Street along the bottom. The factory stands at the Thornton Street end of the block next to Prospect Street: a group of one to three storey brick and frame buildings with forming, blowing, sizing, stiffening, blocking, trimming, finishing, flanging and shipping rooms, a boiler and engine room and a pump, with a small brook entering from the west. Two frame storage sheds stand near Westcott Street. A long note at the left records the factory's watchman, Eimhauser clock, steam power and heat, gas lights, coal fuel, a well and brook water supply with linen hose, and a Worthington fire pump. The dash-dot boundary of the City of East Orange crosses the inset diagonally. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches are marked in Westcott, Thornton and Prospect Streets, and the drawn width of each street is given as 50 feet.
notes: Placed from Thornton / Westcott and Thornton / Prospect (detected) and two block corners carried from sheet 44; the inset is drawn about 13 degrees from sheet 44's orientation.

Midland Av, Ashland Av, Linden Av, Clinton, Washington Av (= Washington Street); Glen Ridge / Bloomfield line. 50 ft, north to the right. Three parts: 1 main; 2 inset (lower centre) Ellor Bros & Hall hat works at Westcott/Thornton/Prospect; 3 inset (lower right) The Nitram Co on Peloubet / E. Maolis Av / Orange. Both insets enlarge areas of sheet 44.

sheet-38-3.description: Part 3 of sheet 38 is an inset at the lower right of the sheet, behind a heavy line, showing The Nitram Co. (Rob. Martin, president and manager), makers of knit novelties, in the Watsessing district of Bloomfield. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch, an enlargement of the block that sheet 44 labels Nitram Novelty Wks, with north pointing roughly to the right. Peloubet Street runs down the left side of the inset and East Maolis Avenue down the right side; Orange runs along the bottom, and Lake Street comes in at the top right. The works occupy the middle of the block: an L-shaped one-storey vacant building and a case storage building along the north and east, a two-storey weaving building with a gas engine and hose connection, a water tank, and a small brick chimney with an underground passage toward Orange. A note at the top records no watchman, gas engine power, steam heat, gas lights and fuel, city water, water pails, Good Due fire annihilators and a 5000 gallon water tank. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches and street widths of 50 and 55 feet are marked. Adjoining sheets are named in the margins: 44 to the west, 42 to the east and 61 south of Orange.
notes: East Maolis Avenue and Orange are today's Orange Street (north and south of the Hill Street junction); Peloubet Street no longer exists.
Placed by a helmert from three block corners along Orange carried from sheet 44; low confidence.

Midland Av, Ashland Av, Linden Av, Clinton, Washington Av (= Washington Street); Glen Ridge / Bloomfield line. 50 ft, north to the right. Three parts: 1 main; 2 inset (lower centre) Ellor Bros & Hall hat works at Westcott/Thornton/Prospect; 3 inset (lower right) The Nitram Co on Peloubet / E. Maolis Av / Orange. Both insets enlarge areas of sheet 44.

sheet-39.description: Sheet 39 shows a block of housing lots and the streets around it in the Watsessing end of Bloomfield, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned on the page so that north points to the right (the compass rose is at the lower left). Maolis Avenue forms the left edge and Linden Avenue the right edge; Clinton runs across the top and Glenwood Avenue across the bottom. Thomas runs through the middle of the sheet between Maolis and Linden Avenues, and 2nd Street leaves Thomas at the lower right and meets Glenwood Avenue, dividing the southern strip into two groups of lots. Almost everything built is a detached frame dwelling of two or two and a half stories, set on narrow lots that run back from the street; the largest groups stand along the Glenwood Avenue frontage, where the lots are lettered A to L, and on Linden Avenue. A bakery with a brick oven stands at the Linden Avenue and Glenwood Avenue corner, where a fire alarm box is marked, and a store with a pink (brick) front stands on Glenwood Avenue near 2nd Street. The northern lots between Clinton and Thomas are mostly open ground with a few outbuildings and a larger house with a shed. Water pipes of 4, 5 and 6 inches are marked in Clinton, Thomas, Linden and Glenwood, with street widths of 50 to 66 feet. A short stub of Hancock Street is lettered at the left margin. Neighbouring sheets are numbered in the margins: 37 above Clinton, 43 at the left, 40 at the right and 42 below Glenwood Avenue.
notes: Maolis Av. is today's Maolis Avenue and Linden Av. is today's Linden Avenue.
Clinton, Thomas and 2nd Street are today's Clinton Street, Thomas Street and 2nd Street.
Hancock Street is not in the modern street data.
50 ft, north right. Block between Maolis Av, Clinton, Linden Av and Glenwood Av with Thomas and 2nd St.

sheet-40-1.description: Part 1 is the main map of sheet 40 and fills the upper and left part of the sheet, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north to the right (the compass rose stands just beyond the heavy dividing line). It lies on the eastern edge of the Watsessing district of Bloomfield. Clinton runs across the top of the part from Linden Avenue at the left to Washington Avenue at the upper right, and Thomas crosses the part below it; Linden Avenue forms the left edge and Henry crosses the lower left. A short length of Glenwood Avenue crosses the bottom left corner. Washington Avenue curves along the right side from the top of the sheet to Thomas St. near the right margin, where a fire alarm box is marked. The ground between Clinton and Thomas is mostly open back land with a row of detached frame dwellings on the Clinton frontage and another row on Thomas; Washington Avenue has a line of dwellings with a few sheds. The lower left block between Linden Avenue and Henry holds more dwellings, and at its southern end A. Loppacker's auto repairing and machine shop, a gasoline-engine shop lit by electricity, is described in a note at the bottom left. Water mains of 4 and 6 inches are marked in the streets. A heavy line from the top right corner running diagonally to the bottom edge separates this part from part 2, a larger-scale drawing of the Glenwood Avenue and Bloomfield Avenue area drawn with north up. Adjoining sheets named in the margins are 38 at the top, 39 at the left, 31 and 46 at the right and 42 below.
notes: Linden Av. is today's Linden Avenue, Clinton and Thomas are today's Clinton Street and Thomas Street, and Henry is today's Henry Street.
Washington Av. is today's Washington Street.
A heavy line divides this part from part 2, which is drawn with north up.

50 ft. Part 1 main (Clinton, Thomas, Linden Av, Henry, Washington Av); part 2 inset lower right across a heavy line (Glenwood Av, Washington Av, Bloomfield Av, north up), anchored on two hand-picked junctions (low). Conger St left out (drawn with a dog-leg).

sheet-40-2.description: Part 2 is the lower right section of sheet 40, set off by a heavy dividing line, and covers the business frontage where Glenwood Avenue, Washington Avenue and Bloomfield Avenue meet near the Bloomfield railroad station. Unlike part 1 it is drawn with north up (a north arrow stands near the right margin), at 50 feet to an inch. Glenwood Avenue runs diagonally from the lower left to the upper right; Washington Avenue runs across the top to Bloomfield Avenue, which runs down the right side. Conger lies along the bottom margin. The long block between Glenwood and Bloomfield Avenues is the most built-up area on the sheet and is coloured as brick and frame business buildings. It holds Scheuers' gas and stable premises, an ice cream manufacturer, an undertaker's premises (Chas. R. Keyler), a real estate office, a bakery, a barber, an upholsterer and a saloon, with cement and feed storage sheds along the south side belonging to Ogden and Cadmus, dealers in feed, brick and cement, whose note lists a furnace in the office and electric lights. A police station and a group of small buildings stand at the lower left near Glenwood Avenue. Water pipes of 4, 6 and 12 inches are marked. Lot numbers on Glenwood Avenue run in the 280s to 310s and on Bloomfield Avenue in the 400s to 550s. Adjoining sheets named in the margins are 41, 42, 45, 46 and 40 (the main part).
notes: Drawn with north up, about 80 degrees from part 1 of the same sheet.
Conger is drawn with a bend that today's Conger Street does not have, so it was not used for control.
Placed from two hand-picked junctions at Washington Avenue (low confidence).

50 ft. Part 1 main (Clinton, Thomas, Linden Av, Henry, Washington Av); part 2 inset lower right across a heavy line (Glenwood Av, Washington Av, Bloomfield Av, north up), anchored on two hand-picked junctions (low). Conger St left out (drawn with a dog-leg).

sheet-41.description: Sheet 41 covers the industrial strip along the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad's Montclair Branch in Bloomfield, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north to the top. The railroad crosses the sheet from the upper left to the lower right as a bundle of parallel tracks, with Mechanic lettered beside it. Washington Avenue appears twice, as the diagonal street at the left and as the street along the top; Farrand Street joins it at the top and Thomas runs down the left side, with Henry along the bottom and Glenwood at the right. Toney's Brook crosses the lower left with a bend and runs down to the lower right. The sheet is dominated by two works: the Hedden Iron Construction Co., whose beam, machine and storage buildings stand in the centre, and the American Malleables Co., an iron foundry with furnace house, pattern shop and pattern storage, shown in pink (brick) at the lower right, with a long note on watchman, fuel, lights and fire appliances. The Bloomfield railroad station stands beside the tracks at the right. Along the right edge a row of shops with a Bloomfield Citizen printing room faces Bloomfield Avenue. Detached dwellings stand along Washington Avenue and in the lower left block between Thomas and Henry. A compass rose at the upper left shows north to the top. Adjoining sheets named in the margins are 27, 28, 40 and 42.
notes: No street named Mechanic is in the modern street data.
Washington Av. is today's Washington Street; Thomas, Henry and Glenwood are today's Thomas Street, Henry Street and Glenwood Avenue.
The street label 'AV.' at the right edge lacks its name on this sheet.
50 ft, north up. Montclair Branch, Hedden Iron Construction Co, American Malleables Co; Thomas, Henry, Washington Av, Farrand St. Exact three-point fit (low-medium).

sheet-42.description: Sheet 42 is drawn at 100 feet to an inch, with north to the right, and covers the district south of Glenwood Avenue between the Second River and Bloomfield Avenue. Glenwood Avenue crosses the top from left to right, meeting 2nd Street, Linden Avenue and Henry Street from the north, and runs on to Conger Street at the upper right. The Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad's Montclair Branch crosses the sheet as a broad band of tracks from the lower left to the upper right, with a freight house and coal pockets in the centre. The Second River crosses at the left centre and Toney's Brook and its west branch join it near the tracks. Along Glenwood Avenue there are a few dwellings and the Hudson Rolling Mill (W. S. Benson, manager, makers of dry batteries), the Harper Machine Co. and the contractor G. Bruett. The lower left is a regular grid of narrow house lots on Lake Street, Orange and Crown Street, with a pink row of brick houses on Lake Street, the Empire Foundry Co., L. Schleif's brass foundry and a street of frame dwellings. East of Crown Street the Franklin House and other buildings front the diagonal Bloomfield Avenue, with Race Street running off it; the scale bar of 100 feet stands at the lower right. East Maolis Avenue and Hill Street run along the left margin. Adjoining sheets named in the margins are 38, 39, 40, 41, 44, 45 and 61.
notes: Second Street is today's 2nd Street; Linden Av. is today's Linden Avenue.
Orange is today's Orange Street; part of the Lake Street and Orange area was rebuilt as John F. Kennedy Drive and the Garden State Parkway.
Orange Street junctions were 2 to 5 m off the modern line.
100 ft, north right. Glenwood Av to Bloomfield Av with the Second River, Lake St, Orange, Crown St; detector min_width_ratio 0.7.

sheet-43.description: Sheet 43 is drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north to the top and shows a thinly built district on the boundary between Bloomfield and Glen Ridge. Midland Avenue runs down the left side of the sheet and the dash-dot boundary of Glen Ridge Borough and the Town of Bloomfield runs parallel to it a short distance to the east. Maolis Avenue crosses the top. A regular grid of streets fills the central part: Ashland Avenue, Putnam Avenue and Hancock Street run south from Maolis Avenue, Llewellyn Avenue crosses them in the middle, and Fulton Avenue, Morse Avenue and Franklin Avenue run south from Llewellyn Avenue to Brighton Avenue, Carteret Street and, further on, the line of the City of East Orange at the bottom. Columbus Avenue runs south from Carteret Street. Glenwood Avenue and Prospect Street are at the right edge with the Second River winding down beside them. The numbers 1 to 5 mark the blocks of the lot plan. Very little is built: a handful of dwellings between Midland Avenue and Ashland Avenue near Maolis Avenue and two short rows on Llewellyn Avenue near Putnam and Hancock, with one more dwelling near Carteret Street and two near the right edge; all the rest is unbuilt lots. Street widths of 50, 60, 66 and 70 feet are marked, with 6 inch water pipes in Maolis Avenue and Midland Avenue. Adjoining sheets named in the margins are 37, 39, 34, 14, 33 and 44.
notes: Fulton Av. between Llewellyn and Brighton is today's North Fulton Street.
Morse Avenue lies about 5 m from the modern Morse Avenue and was not used for control.
Llewellyn Av. is today's Llewellyn Avenue.
The sheet carries the title Bloomfield and Glen Ridge at the top.
100 ft. Maolis Av to Carteret St grid on the Glen Ridge boundary, Midland Av. Morse Av left out (4-6 m off).

sheet-44.description: Sheet 44 covers the Watsessing district in the southwest of Bloomfield at 100 feet to an inch, turned so that north points to the right. Prospect Street crosses the upper part of the sheet, with Westcott Street and Thornton Street at the upper left, Glenwood Avenue and Carteret Street at the top, and Maolis Avenue meeting Glenwood Avenue at the upper right beside Glenwood Park, which has a dancing pavilion. Below Prospect Street, Olive Street, Myrtle Avenue, Willow Street and Locust Avenue run down the sheet toward Orange along the bottom, crossed by Hinrich Place, Dodd Street, Nelson Street and Filbert Street; Langdon Street, Peloubet Street and East Maolis Avenue lie in the lower right, with Lake Street at the right edge, and Lawrence Street and Harlow Street meet Dodd Street at the lower left. Cross Street and Hill Street lead south from Orange. The Second River crosses from Glenwood Park to the east edge, and a brook runs through the blocks between Myrtle Avenue and Willow Street. The D. L. & W. R. R. Montclair Branch crosses the lower part diagonally. The district is mostly frame dwellings on narrow lots, with Watsessing School No. 8 on Prospect Street, F. J. North beer bottling, The National Label Press on Myrtle Avenue, the Empire Cream Separator Co. and Ampere Silk Mill beside the railroad (see sheet 35), Nitram Novelty Works (see sheet 38) and Ellor Bros. & Hall hat works (see sheet 38). The City of East Orange line runs down the left edge.
notes: Myrtle Avenue is today's Myrtle Street; Hinrich Place is Hinrichs Place (realigned: Dodd / Hinrichs rejected at 11 m).

East Maolis Avenue and Orange are today's Orange Street; Hill Street keeps its name. Nelson, Filbert, Langdon and Peloubet Streets are gone (John F. Kennedy Drive and the Garden State Parkway cross the district).
Willow Street now curves to Orange Street; that junction was left out.
Glen Ridge 1907 sheet 35 shows the Empire Cream Separator Co. and Ampere Silk Mill at a larger scale.

Watsessing district (catalogued with Glen Ridge but not in glen-ridge-1907). Prospect St, Westcott, Thornton, Glenwood Av, Maolis Av, Locust Av, Willow St, Myrtle Av, Olive St, Hinrich Pl, Dodd St, Nelson, Filbert, Langdon, Peloubet, E. Maolis Av, Orange; Glenwood Park, Second River; DL&W Montclair Branch. 100 ft, north to the right. One part.

sheet-45-1.description: Part 1 is the left half of sheet 45, divided from part 2 by a heavy line that runs down the sheet, and is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north pointing to the upper right (the compass rose is at the top). It lies on the west side of Bloomfield Avenue in the centre of Bloomfield. Bloomfield Avenue runs down the left edge; Washington Avenue leaves it at the top and runs south-east along a line of detached dwellings, with Franklin Street joining it and running down the right side of the part. Race crosses the bottom, and Montgomery Street meets Franklin Street near the middle with a fire alarm box. At the top the pointed corner of the Bloomfield Avenue and Washington Avenue block is filled with shops, among them a confectioner, a photographer, an office, barbers, a laundry, plumbing and tinning, paper stock and a fish dealer, with a cobbler and a paint shop beside them on Washington Avenue. The centre is a large grounds with a large house, curved drives and a path, and the lower part holds detached dwellings on Race and Bloomfield Avenue. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches and street widths of 50, 66 and 80 feet are marked. Conger St. is lettered at the left margin. Adjoining sheets named in the margins are 40, 42, 45, 46 and 57.
notes: Race is today's Burroughs Place.
Washington Av. is today's Washington Street; Franklin and Franklin St. are today's Franklin Street.
Bloomfield Avenue and Washington Avenue meet just above the top edge of the part.

50 ft, two parts across a heavy line: 1 left (Bloomfield Av, Washington Av, Franklin St, Race = Burroughs Place), 2 right (Bloomfield Av, Race, Orange, Franklin); the parts differ in rotation by 15 degrees.

sheet-45-2.description: Part 2 is the right half of sheet 45, divided from part 1 by a heavy line. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north to the top (a compass rose near the lower right) and shows the east side of Bloomfield Avenue in the centre of Bloomfield. Bloomfield Avenue runs down the left of the part beside the heavy line; Race crosses the top, Orange crosses the lower part and Newark Av. leaves it near the right margin, where Franklin runs down the right edge. The Second River crosses the part from the left centre to the right edge as a blue band under a bridge on Bloomfield Avenue. A row of detached frame dwellings faces Race, with larger outbuildings behind them, and Jas. Crisp and Son, sewing machine belting, occupy a long building near the river whose note lists city water, chemical fire extinguishers and electric light. South of the river are a news shop and a group of buildings on Bloomfield Avenue that includes a hotel with a dance hall, a cobbler, a barber and a fruit store. The lower half of the part is mostly open ground on Orange. A fire alarm box stands at the Bloomfield Avenue and Orange junction. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches and widths of 40 to 80 feet are marked. Adjoining sheets named in the margins are 42, 45, 57 and 59.
notes: Race is today's Burroughs Place; Orange is today's Orange Street.
Newark Av. is today's Newark Avenue.
Placed from detected junctions on Bloomfield Avenue, Race and Franklin.

50 ft, two parts across a heavy line: 1 left (Bloomfield Av, Washington Av, Franklin St, Race = Burroughs Place), 2 right (Bloomfield Av, Race, Orange, Franklin); the parts differ in rotation by 15 degrees.

sheet-46.description: This sheet shows the centre of Bloomfield around the junction of Broad Street, Franklin Street and Washington Avenue, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north close to the top of the page. Liberty Street runs along the top edge, Broad Street along the left edge, Oakland Avenue down the right edge and Montgomery Street across the bottom right corner. Franklin Street crosses the sheet diagonally from the upper left to the bottom, with Fremont Street and Austin Place meeting it and each other in the middle of the sheet, and Washington Avenue running off to the lower left. The west side, along Broad Street, is the commercial frontage: a row of small stores including a grocery, barber, tailor, automobile and sporting goods dealers, a cobbler and a bakery, the American House hotel with a pool room, the Hotel Essex, the Bloomfield Livery stable with its hotel sheds, and the Savings Institute and Trust Co. Near Franklin Street and Washington Avenue stand the First Baptist Church and its Sunday school. The middle and east of the sheet are mainly frame dwellings on large lots, interrupted by the Westminster Presbyterian Church, the Jarvie Memorial Church and Library with its Sunday school, St. John's German Lutheran Church on Austin Place, and the Newark German Theological School near Liberty Street. Water mains of 4 and 6 inches are marked along the streets, overhead wire poles and fire alarm boxes are shown, and a cement covered building stands on the east side of Franklin Street. Neighbouring sheets 24, 47, 49, 57, 45 and 40 are indicated at the margins.
notes: Washington Avenue is today Washington Street.
Liberty, Fremont, Franklin, Austin Place, Oakland Avenue and Montgomery are today Liberty Street, Fremont Street, Franklin Street, Austin Place, Oakland Avenue and Montgomery Street.

Franklin Street / Washington Street was not detected: the drawn junction is irregular where Franklin Street widens, so the lower part of the sheet rests on the Fremont, Oakland and Montgomery junctions.
Printed scale bar and fitted scale agree with 50 feet to an inch.
50 ft. Broad, Franklin, Washington Av, Fremont, Austin Pl, Oakland Av; centre of Bloomfield. Franklin/Washington left out.

sheet-47.description: Sheet 47 shows one long residential block and its frontages in central Bloomfield, east of the Green. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned on the page, with north pointing to the right. Park Place runs across the top of the sheet and Spruce Street across the bottom; Liberty Street forms the left (west) edge and Beach Street the right (east) edge. Monroe Place runs through the middle of the block between Park Place and Spruce Street, splitting it into two halves of house lots. Short cross streets only touch the edges: Austin Place and Oakland Road meet Liberty Street on the left, and Elm Street and Oak Street meet Beach Street on the right; each continues on the neighbouring sheets (46, 48 and 49). The block is almost entirely detached frame dwellings with stables and outbuildings set back on deep lots, many of them on Monroe Place. The one large public building is the Bloomfield Center School, a brick school on the Liberty Street side near Austin Place, coloured pink. The northern half of the block toward Park Place has larger houses on wider lots; the southern half toward Spruce Street is more open, with several vacant lots. Water mains and hydrants are marked in the surrounding streets. Adjoining sheets are numbered in the margins: 24 above Park Place, 46 and 49 to the west, 48 to the east and 51 below Spruce Street. The sheet carries the scale bar at the bottom left and a compass rose near the middle of the block.
notes: Oakland Road is today's Oakland Avenue.
Bloomfield Center School stands on the Liberty Street side of the block.
Pilot. Park Pl, Spruce, Liberty, Beach, Monroe Pl; Bloomfield Center School. 50 ft, north to the right. One part.

sheet-48.description: This sheet covers a strip of Bloomfield north and east of the town centre, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north is to the right of the page. Broad Street runs along the top edge, Belleville Avenue down the right side, Beach Street down the left side and Spruce Street along the bottom, with Elm Street and Oak Street crossing the sheet as two horizontal streets and Church Street running between Broad Street and Elm Street in the upper half. A short Park Place enters from the left near the top. The upper block is occupied by the First Presbyterian Church, dated 1796, with its Sunday school, a parish house and several dwellings, and by the Bloomfield High School, a large brick and frame building with its own heating and lighting notes, on the Belleville Avenue side. The lower blocks between Elm Street and Oak Street hold frame dwellings on wide lots, with a few outbuildings and a large stable or tenement building near Oak Street. At the bottom right the Erie Railroad Greenwood Lake Division crosses the sheet diagonally between Oak Street and Spruce Street, and a tool house stands beside it. Below Oak Street a small block of dwellings and sheds lies between Beach Street and the railroad. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches run along the streets and a fire alarm box stands at the corner of Belleville Avenue and Oak Street. Adjoining sheets 24, 23, 19, 47 and 52 are named in the margins. The compass on the sheet confirms the turned orientation.
notes: The page is turned: north points to the right.
The Erie Railroad Greenwood Lake Division shown here is abandoned today.
Street names keep their names today as Street (Elm Street, Oak Street) and Belleville Avenue.
50 ft, north right. Broad, Church, Elm, Oak, Spruce, Beach, Belleville Av; Erie Greenwood Lake Division.

sheet-49.description: This sheet shows the west bank of the Morris Canal in Bloomfield, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north close to the top. Oakland Avenue runs diagonally down the left side, Liberty Street along the top, Montgomery Street along the bottom, and Fremont Street and Spruce Street cross each other in the middle of the sheet. The Morris Canal, with its tow path, runs down the right centre of the sheet; at the lower end a lock and a small branch channel appear near Montgomery Street, where the canal passes under the street. East of the canal, Hickory Street, Sycamore Street, Vine Street and Vine Place run through a district of small lots. West of the canal the blocks between Oakland Avenue and Spruce Street are filled with frame dwellings, and a factory yard stands on Spruce Street. At the foot of Spruce Street, beside the canal, are the Bloomfield Coal and Supply Co. with its coal pockets fifty feet high, wood piles, an engine house and a wood sawing shed in green. A lower row of dwellings fronts Montgomery Street. Water mains of 4 and 6 inches follow the streets, and fire alarm boxes and overhead wire poles are marked. Neighbouring sheets 47, 46, 51, 50 and 57 are named at the margins. The district was later cut through by the bed of the canal, which is now the line of the Garden State Parkway.
notes: The Morris Canal bed is now the Garden State Parkway; the canal-side streets east of it have few surviving junctions.
Vine Place is drawn as a 20 foot lane; its junction with Vine Street was not accepted (6.6 m from the fit on sheet 50) and is not used.
Spruce Street is drawn narrower than the modern right of way at Belleville Avenue and Fremont Street.
50 ft. Oakland Av, Fremont, Spruce, Liberty, Montgomery west of the Morris Canal; Hickory, Sycamore, Vine east of it.

sheet-50.description: This sheet covers a residential district east of the Morris Canal in Bloomfield, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north close to the top. Liberty Street runs along the top edge and Montgomery Street along the bottom; Hickory Street and Walnut Street run down the left and centre, Stockton Street runs south from Walnut Terrace towards Montgomery Street, and Williamson Avenue runs down the right edge. Sycamore Street and Vine Street cross the left half, and Vine Place, a narrow lane, lies at the left edge beside the canal strip. Walnut Terrace crosses the sheet near the middle from Walnut Street to Williamson Avenue. The blocks are mostly frame dwellings on lots with barns and outbuildings. At the top left stands the turf goods and machine shop of Spear and Co., with its stock room and machine room, and carpenter shops appear in two of the blocks, one with a stable near Montgomery Street. A diagonal lot line cuts across the block between Walnut Street and Stockton Street. A fire alarm box is shown at the lower right corner. Water mains of 4 and 6 inches follow the streets. The compass on the sheet shows north tilted slightly to the right. Neighbouring sheets 49, 51, 54 and 57 are named at the margins. Part of the Morris Canal appears at the extreme left edge, where this sheet overlaps sheet 49.
notes: Sycamore, Vine, Hickory, Walnut and Stockton are printed without suffix; today they are Sycamore Street, Vine Street, Hickory Street, Walnut Street and Stockton Street.
Vine Place / Vine Street was detected 6.6 m from the fit and rejected; Vine Place is not at its modern line.
Stockton Street is drawn on a slant; its junction with Montgomery Street was used.
50 ft. Hickory, Walnut, Stockton, Williamson Av between Liberty and Montgomery; Vine Place rejected (6.6 m).

sheet-51.description: This sheet shows the Morris Canal crossing Bloomfield with the Erie Railroad Greenwood Lake Division beside Walnut Street, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north is to the right. Spruce Street runs along the top edge and Williamson Avenue along the bottom; Liberty Street runs down the left side, Walnut Street crosses the middle of the sheet from left to right, and Mulberry Street runs a short way south of the canal parallel to Liberty Street. Beach Street runs up to the right from the Walnut Street junction past the Walnut Street Passenger Station, and Hazelwood Road runs down the right side. Across the top, north of the canal, are dwellings and the works of the Jas. E. Brooks Co., structural steel workers, with machine room, pattern room and a boiler plant. The Morris Canal with its two channels crosses the sheet from left to right, with road bridges at Liberty Street and Beach Street. Below the canal the large central block is vacant, and a row of dwellings fronts Walnut Street. South of Walnut Street lies the lumber yard and sheds of Chas. J. Murray, with a freight station and the tracks and sidings of the Erie Railroad Greenwood Lake Division running diagonally to the right. Hickory Street meets Liberty Street at the left edge. Water mains and overhead wires are marked. Neighbouring sheets 47, 50, 52 and 53 appear at the margins.
notes: Mulberry Street is not in the modern street data and was not used.
The Erie Railroad Greenwood Lake Division is abandoned; the Morris Canal bed is now the Garden State Parkway.
The sheet is turned: north points to the right.
Spruce Street at the top edge is a boundary street; its junction with Liberty Street rests on one drawn edge and a parcel width.
50 ft, north right. Morris Canal, Walnut, Beach, Hazelwood Rd, Liberty, Williamson Av, Erie Greenwood Lake Division.

sheet-52.description: This sheet shows the north-east edge of Bloomfield where Walnut Street, Beach Street and Hazelwood Road meet the Erie Railroad and the Morris Canal, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north is to the right. Spruce Street runs along the top, Williamson Avenue along the bottom, Belleville Avenue down the right side and Hazelwood Road down the left, with Beach Street entering at the upper left and Walnut Street crossing the middle from left to right. The Morris Canal and its tow path cross the upper part of the sheet, with a bridge at Belleville Avenue, and the Erie Railroad Greenwood Lake Division runs diagonally from the top centre to the lower left past the Walnut Street Passenger Station, which stands on a triangular island between Beach Street and the tracks. A short row of dwellings, one tinted blue for a different construction, fronts Spruce Street at the top. The large block between Walnut Street and the canal holds a few scattered dwellings, among them a large house marked Stone Ho. near Belleville Avenue, with open ground beyond. South of Walnut Street the blocks between Hazelwood Road and Belleville Avenue hold dwellings, stables and outbuildings, with a fire alarm box at the corner of Belleville Avenue near the bottom. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches follow the streets. A private driveway enters from Belleville Avenue. The compass shows north to the right, and sheets 48, 51, 53 and 20 are named at the margins.
notes: The sheet is turned: north points to the right.
Belleville Avenue / Spruce Street is flagged narrow: Spruce Street is drawn narrower than today's right of way.
Only five control points were found; Hazelwood Road / Walnut Street was not detected, so leave-one-out is 4.4 m.
The Greenwood Lake Division and the Morris Canal bed are no longer in place.
50 ft, north right. Spruce, Beach, Walnut, Hazelwood Rd, Williamson Av, Belleville Av, canal and Erie.

sheet-53.description: Sheet 53 covers a residential district in the northwest of Bloomfield, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north pointing a little to the right of the page vertical. Belleville Avenue crosses the upper part of the sheet from the upper left to the right edge, bending slightly to the east about two thirds of the way across. Williamson Avenue runs down the left side, Clarendon Place runs south from Belleville Avenue through the middle of the sheet, and Orchard runs down the right side. Hazelwood Road leaves Williamson Avenue below the middle, passes beneath Clarendon Place's foot and curves east to meet Orchard, where a short street named Baylis is lettered at the right margin. Berkeley Avenue enters at the bottom edge and Liberty runs along the foot of the sheet. The blocks are lined with detached two and a half storey frame dwellings on large lots, with a few sheds, hen houses and an auto house, and a brick pit is marked beside the lot lines west of Clarendon Place. Five houses of identical plan stand in a row along the east side of the block at the lower right. The Erie Railroad, Greenwood Lake Division, crosses the lower part of the sheet from upper left to lower right as two pairs of rails in a wide strip; there is no station on this sheet. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches run down the middle of the streets, and a fire alarm box stands at the top left and drinking-hydrant marks are scattered along the street edges. Adjoining sheets are numbered in the margins: 20 above, 52 and 51 to the west, 10 above Belleville Avenue, 55 to the east and 54 below.
notes: Baylis Street, lettered at the right margin beside Orchard, is today's eastern part of Hazelwood Road (see sheet 55, where the street is drawn as Baylis).
Orchard and Liberty are lettered without a suffix; the modern streets are Orchard Street and Liberty Street.
The Erie Railroad Greenwood Lake Division is abandoned and has no current line in the street data; it was not used as control.
Belleville Avenue / Williamson Avenue lies about 36 ft beyond the top of the sheet and was not detected.
50 ft. Belleville Av, Williamson Av, Clarendon Pl, Hazelwood Road; Erie Greenwood Lake Division.

sheet-54.description: Sheet 54 covers a thinly built part of northwest Bloomfield between Liberty at the top and Montgomery at the foot, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north pointing to the upper right. Williamson Avenue runs down the left side, Berkeley Avenue down the middle and Orchard down the right side, so the sheet is made up of two long north-south blocks between three parallel streets. The block between Williamson Avenue and Berkeley Avenue is largely open: large undivided tracts occupy most of it, with a few frame dwellings and hen houses along its edges and clustered at the lower left, where a group of dwellings and a pair of outbuildings stand beside Montgomery. The Fairview Public School, a brick building heated by steam and lit by gas and electricity, with a front addition marked as drawn from plans, stands near the foot of Berkeley Avenue and is coloured pink. The block between Berkeley Avenue and Orchard is divided into narrow, regular lots, and a continuous row of detached two and a half storey frame dwellings faces Orchard down its whole length. At the top right corner the sheet shows the edge of the Erie Railroad, Greenwood Lake Division, which crosses the corner diagonally. Walnut Terrace is lettered at the left edge and a compass rose with a north arrow stands at the left margin. Four-inch water pipes run in the centre of Williamson Avenue and Orchard, and fire alarm boxes and hydrants are marked at the corners. Adjoining sheets are numbered in the margins: 53 above, 50 and 57 to the west and southwest, and 56 below.
notes: Liberty, Orchard and Montgomery are lettered without a suffix; the modern streets are Liberty Street, Orchard Street and Montgomery Street.
Berkeley Avenue / Montgomery Street lies at the foot of the sheet and was not detected; the part is placed from four junctions.
50 ft. Williamson, Berkeley, Orchard between Liberty and Montgomery; Fairview School; mostly open. 4 points.

sheet-55.description: Sheet 55 covers the northwest corner of Bloomfield at 50 feet to an inch, with north pointing straight up. Belleville Avenue crosses the top of the sheet from the upper left to the right edge, bending southeast at about the middle. Orchard runs down the left side with a slight lean to the right and meets Baylis near the middle of the sheet, where Hazelwood Road, lettered on the left margin, continues to sheet 53. Smith and Davey run down the sheet from Belleville Avenue to Liberty, and the block between Davey and the right edge is open ground. Houses along Orchard are two and a half storey frame dwellings on regular lots with outbuildings behind. The block between Orchard and Smith carries the largest houses, and its lots run down to Baylis. On the right, two blocks lie between Smith and Davey, and a short row of small dwellings, marked A, B and 7, fronts Liberty. The Erie Railroad, Greenwood Lake Division, crosses the lower part of the sheet from upper left to lower right as two pairs of rails in a wide strip; the Orchard Street passenger station, a one and a half storey frame building, stands beside the track at the foot of Orchard. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches run down the street centres and a fire alarm box stands near the station. A north arrow and compass rose are placed at the lower left. Adjoining sheets are numbered in the margins: 53 to the west, 10 above, 56 to the east and below.
notes: Baylis is today's eastern part of Hazelwood Road; Liberty east of Smith is today's East Liberty Street.
Orchard, Smith, Davey, Baylis and Liberty are lettered without a suffix; the modern streets are Orchard Street, Smith Street, Davey Street and East Liberty Street.
Belleville Avenue / Davey Street is two modern nodes about 25 m apart; the detector found the junction once only.
A small hand-lettered date at the lower right corner is partly illegible (reads something like II/5/07) and was not recorded.
50 ft. Belleville Av, Orchard, Baylis (= Hazelwood Road), Smith, Davey, Liberty (= East Liberty Street); Erie RR.

sheet-56.description: Sheet 56 covers the northwest part of Bloomfield around the Morris Canal and the Second River, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned about 13 degrees from the page vertical. The upper part repeats the streets of sheet 55: Baylis, Smith, Davey and Liberty in the upper left, with Belleville Avenue across the top and Morton Street and John Street running down toward the middle, and Willett Street and Mill Street at the right. The Erie Railroad, Greenwood Lake Division, crosses the sheet from left to right just below the middle of the upper block as a wide strip of tracks. South of it a long block between Orchard and John Street is filled with narrow lots, a row of dwellings along Orchard and Montgomery, and a large nursery group of glass houses lettered J. Hauck, Florist, and J. J. Brozat, Florist. Montgomery crosses the sheet from lower left to upper right and meets Mill Street and Willett Street at the right edge beside the canal. The Second River winds across the lower middle in a loop and runs beside the Morris Canal with its tow path, both drawn as blue bands, and the canal crosses Berkeley Avenue on a bridge at the foot of the sheet. Brighton Avenue and Harrison Street cross the unbuilt ground at the lower right, and Weaver Avenue and Cedar Street enter at the bottom. A dash-dot township line runs down the right side of the sheet, lettered with the names Belleville and Township, and the right margin carries a sideways note that appears to read See Volume One. The scale bar and a compass rose stand at the left margin. Adjoining sheets 53, 54, 55, 57 and 58 are numbered in the margins.
notes: Baylis Street is today's eastern part of Hazelwood Road; Liberty Street east of Smith Street is today's East Liberty Street.
Willett Street is spelled Willett in the street data and Willet on some modern maps; the sheet's spelling is kept.
The Morris Canal bed is now the Garden State Parkway; the Second River is drawn in a loop that no longer exists.
The margin note at the right edge is lettered sideways in pieces and reads See Volume One with medium confidence.
St. James Pl. is printed on the township line (written out as Saint James Place); it has no junction in the street data.
100 ft. Morris Canal and Second River, Montgomery, John, Willett, Mill; Hauck and Brozat florists.

sheet-57.description: Sheet 57 covers the district of Bloomfield between Montgomery Street and Newark Avenue, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned about 82 degrees, so that Montgomery Street runs down the left side of the page and Berkeley Avenue across the top. The left third is a built-up residential area of detached two and a half storey frame dwellings fronting Montgomery Street and Jerome Place, with Walnut Street and West Street crossing at right angles and Race Street, Spruce Street, Stockton Street and Oakland Avenue leading off. At the top, the Ascension Chapel of the Protestant Episcopal church stands on Berkeley Avenue near Williamson Avenue, and the Montgomery Hose Company No. 4, a volunteer fire company with a hose house and cart, stands at the head of Jerome Place. Two long rows of narrow lots run east from Jerome Place to the canal. The Morris Canal and the Second River run through the middle of the sheet as blue bands: the canal enters at the top, bends below Walnut Street, runs west along West Street past a coal pile and scales, and the river runs on down the sheet beside Newark Avenue to Franklin Street. At the foot of the sheet, a row of attached brick dwellings stands along Oakland Avenue and another row along Franklin Street.
