The east half is more open ground with a few houses along Newark Avenue, Fairview Avenue, Berkeley Avenue, Franklin Street and Berkeley Place; a large brick building, tinted pink, stands near the centre. A north arrow and compass rose stand at the lower right, with the scale bar. Adjoining sheets 54, 50, 49, 46, 45, 56, 58, 59 and 60 are numbered in the margins.
notes: Newark Avenue is drawn 100 ft wide; the modern Newark Avenue centre line lies about 11 m east of the drawn centre, and junctions with it carried residuals of 3 to 4 m, so Newark Avenue was left out of the control.
Montgomery Street south of West Street: the modern Montgomery Street and the Garden State Parkway cut diagonally through the lower left of the sheet, where the drawn street runs straight.
The Morris Canal bed is now the Garden State Parkway.
Willard Avenue is read with medium confidence at full resolution; the last letters are cramped against the water pipe.
The date or initials at the lower right corner were not recorded.
100 ft, turned -82. Montgomery, Jerome, Walnut, West, Race, canal, Franklin. Newark Av left out (about 11 m off).

sheet-58.description: Sheet 58 covers a thinly built district of Bloomfield between Cedar Street at the top and Franklin Street at the foot, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned about 21 degrees from the page vertical. Berkeley Avenue runs down the left side of the sheet, with Fairview Avenue entering from the left margin. Weaver Avenue, Baldwin Place and Harrison Street run parallel to it down the sheet from the top, and Salter Place runs down the right side. Newark Avenue, drawn 100 feet wide, crosses the middle of the sheet from left to right and divides it into an upper and a lower district. Franklin Street leaves Berkeley Avenue at the lower left and runs south-east across the bottom of the sheet, with the short Watsessing Avenue leaving it at the foot. The Second River and the Morris Canal appear at the top left corner, crossing Berkeley Avenue on a bridge at Cedar Street. The ground is mostly laid out in long narrow lots, with detached two and a half storey frame dwellings along the streets, scattered outbuildings and coops, and large vacant tracts at the top and bottom right. A narrow strip along the right edge holds a few dwellings and a long yellow shed. A dash-dot line lettered with the words Belleville and Township crosses the sheet from the upper centre to the lower right, and the right margin carries the note See Volume One, which marks the edge of the volume. A compass rose and north arrow stand at the lower left and the scale bar at the foot. Adjoining sheets 56, 57, 60 and 67 are numbered in the margins.
notes: Newark Avenue is drawn 100 ft wide; the modern Newark Avenue line sits several metres from the drawn centre and its junctions carried residuals of 4 to 6 m, so Newark Avenue was left out of the control (the part rests on Cedar, Franklin and Berkeley junctions).
The margin note at the right edge is read as See Volume One with medium confidence, because the words are lettered sideways and in separate pieces.
The Morris Canal bed is now the Garden State Parkway.
100 ft. Berkeley, Weaver, Baldwin Pl, Harrison, Franklin, Salter Pl; See Volume One margin. Newark Av left out.

sheet-59.description: Sheet 59 shows a narrow strip of the Watsessing district of Bloomfield between Orange Street at the top left and Berkeley Place at the foot, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north to the top. Bloomfield Avenue crosses the sheet as a wide diagonal from the upper left to the lower centre, and its west side is left to sheet 61. East of it lies a large, almost empty block: a few detached dwellings stand along the avenue's frontage near Orange Street, a row of small lots with dwellings and outbuildings lies between Franklin Street and Berkeley Place at the upper right, and the Berkeley Public School, drawn in pink with a heating and lighting note, stands near the foot of the sheet. Franklin Street runs across the top from the upper centre to the right edge, and Berkeley Place bounds the block on the east, curving at the bottom to meet Bloomfield Avenue. Hill Street and Ella Street are drawn only as short stubs entering the avenue from the west. Most of the sheet is blank, the ground being unbuilt or covered by neighbouring sheets, and the scale bar and compass rose are in the lower left.
notes: Bloomfield Avenue meets Hill Street and Ella Street on the sheet's west side; both appear only as short stubs.
The blank west part of the sheet is drawn on sheet 61.
50 ft. Bloomfield Av strip; anchored on two hand-picked junctions (low). Berkeley Place/Bloomfield left out.

sheet-60.description: Sheet 60 covers the Berkeley Heights and Halcyon Park area of Bloomfield, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north lies to the right. Berkeley Place runs along the top edge. At the upper left Bloomfield Avenue passes the curving lane called Berkeley Heights Park, and below it Willard Avenue runs across the sheet as a long street lined with narrow building lots, most of them still empty. Berkeley Avenue crosses below it, and Watsessing Avenue follows the left edge before turning south-east along the foot of the sheet. Franklin Street runs down the right edge. The lower half is occupied by Halcyon Park, a landscaped area with a pond and a small lake, bordered by East Parkway and West Parkway, with Vesper Place, Fontaine Avenue, Orchard Place and Farrandale Avenue running north-south and Florence Avenue and Lexington Avenue crossing the park. A club house stands at the east end of the park and a few dwellings face Watsessing Avenue. Dwellings are scattered thinly along Bloomfield Avenue and Berkeley Avenue, and most lots on Willard Avenue are drawn but unbuilt. The scale bar and compass are at the lower edge.
notes: Berkeley Heights Park is lettered on a curved lane, so it may be a street name as well as a park name.
Weaver Avenue is read from a lettering that is small on the scan.
The modern Franklin Street and Willard Avenue junction does not match the drawn one.
100 ft, north right. Berkeley Heights Park, Halcyon Park area: Bloomfield Av, Watsessing Av, Berkeley Av, Fontaine, Florence, Franklin. Franklin/Willard rejected (15 m).

sheet-61.description: Sheet 61 shows the Watsessing district of Bloomfield, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north near the top. The sheet is a wedge between Orange Street on the west and Bloomfield Avenue on the east, which meet at the top near a fire alarm box. Hill Street runs east from Orange Street to Bloomfield Avenue across the upper part, lined with small dwellings, and Crown Street runs off to the north-west. Below it a grid of narrow lots lies between Orange Street, Charles Street, Ella Street, Grace Street and Delaware Avenue, with Cross Street crossing the middle and Watsessing Avenue closing the foot. Almost all the buildings are dwellings of two and a half storeys, with a church, a firehouse and a few stores. Near the top left stand the L. C. Harrison Co. pipe organ works and the Fries Bros. chemical works, both referred to sheets 65 and 62, and the United States Aristotype Co. is drawn at the head of Charles Street with a reference to sheet 62. The Job Haines Home for Aged People stands near the lower right on Watsessing Avenue. At the lower left the Montclair Branch of the D.L.&W. runs past Willow Street and Myrtle Avenue. Berkeley Place and the Berkeley Heights Park lane branch from Bloomfield Avenue on the right.
notes: Charles Street, north of Cross Street, lies about 50 m west of the modern Charles Street line.
The upper part of the drawn Ella Street is Delaware Place today.
Peloubet Street, E. Maolis Street and Willow Street no longer exist in this form.
Contains the Home for Aged People of Job Haines.
100 ft. Watsessing: Orange St, Hill St, Ella, Charles, Cross, Grace, Delaware Av, Watsessing Av, Bloomfield Av. Charles/Delaware Place excluded (modern Charles 50 m off north of Cross).

sheet-62-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 62 is the main map, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north lies to the upper left. It shows the open land of the Watsessing district east of the Erie Railroad Orange Branch. Watsessing Avenue runs from the upper centre down to the left edge, and Bloomfield Avenue crosses from the lower left to the right, meeting Berkeley Avenue and Watsessing Avenue near the left. Grove Street runs from the top centre down to the right and Brookside Place is a short stub off Bloomfield Avenue. The Erie Railroad Orange Branch crosses the sheet near its middle as a bundle of tracks running up the page. At the upper left a few dwellings stand along Watsessing Avenue and Berkeley Avenue, and a short row of small houses stands at the head of the sheet. Arlington Avenue and Clearfield Avenue run diagonally across the lower left but are drawn only as streets with no buildings. The large central area is unbuilt. The part is separated by a heavy line from the inset at the lower right, which shows the Fries Bros. and Aristotype works at 50 feet to an inch.
notes: The scale is 100 feet to an inch.
Grove Street here is the modern Grove Street junction with Bloomfield Avenue.

Two parts: 1 main at 100 ft (Watsessing Av, Berkeley Av, Bloomfield Av, Grove St, Arlington Av); 2 inset lower right at 50 ft: United States Aristotype Co and Fries Bros. saccharine works on Orange / Peloubet / E. Maolis St / Ella / Delaware Av (three hand-picked points).

sheet-62-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 62 is an inset at the lower right, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and marked 50 feet to an inch, showing ground that sheets 61 and 44 draw at 100 feet. It is turned so that north points to the right. Orange Street runs across the top with Peloubet Street and E. Maolis Street meeting it from the north, Hill Street runs down the right side and Charles Street crosses near the foot of the inset's upper block. The largest works are those of Fries Bros., makers of saccharine, drawn at the top with storage buildings, a mill, cement floors and fire apparatus listed in the text beside them. Below them a large brick factory and several small buildings face Hill Street. Lower down stands the United States Aristotype Co. paper works (W. B. Daly, president), a long narrow building with a note of its fire protection. Ella Street crosses near the foot, where a fire alarm box stands at the corner of Delaware Avenue.
notes: Inset at 50 feet to an inch of the area also drawn on sheet 61 at 100 feet.
Placed from three hand-picked street junctions; the fitted scale is 7.99 px/ft.

Two parts: 1 main at 100 ft (Watsessing Av, Berkeley Av, Bloomfield Av, Grove St, Arlington Av); 2 inset lower right at 50 ft: United States Aristotype Co and Fries Bros. saccharine works on Orange / Peloubet / E. Maolis St / Ella / Delaware Av (three hand-picked points).

sheet-63-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 63 is the main map, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the left. Watsessing Avenue runs the full height of the left side, with Grace Street, Ella Street and Charles Street entering it from the west as stubs and Molter Place meeting it at the foot. Clearfield Avenue runs parallel to it, a short way east, and Arlington Avenue crosses the upper middle diagonally. The principal feature is the factory of the Sawyer Mann Electric Co., makers of electric lamps, drawn in blue with a text describing its fire-proof construction: a long main building marked as the first story completed, a storage building and a proposed power house. A short row of small dwellings stands on the west side of Clearfield Avenue and a boarding house stands near Molter Place. The D.L.&W. Montclair Division runs across the foot and the Erie Railroad Orange Branch along the right edge. A few small temporary buildings stand near the factory. Two insets at the top, divided from the main map by heavy lines, show the National Label Press and the E. H. Davey Co. paste-board mill.
notes: Molter Place junction with Watsessing Avenue was left out of the fit: the modern node is about 11 m from the drawn street.
Placed from three points along Watsessing Avenue only; low confidence across the street.

50 ft. Three parts: 1 main (Watsessing Av, Clearfield Av, Arlington Av, Molter Pl; Sawyer Mann Electric Co), helmert along Watsessing Av (low); 2 inset top centre (The National Label Press, Myrtle Av / Hinrich Pl, carried from sheet 44); 3 inset top right (E. H. Davey Co paste-board mill on the Third River) not placed.

sheet-63-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 63 is an inset at the top centre, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper left. It shows the works of The National Label Press (Sam Wild, manager) on Myrtle Avenue at the top, at the same place as sheet 44 draws at 100 feet. The works consist of one large building with a varnish alley, press rooms and a plate foundry, with a shipping room and office to the east, a small engine room with a 40 horse-power engine and a plate storage building. The text at the left lists the night and Sunday watchman, clock stations, fire extinguishers and water pails. Hinrich Place curves along the foot of the inset and a lane runs south from the works. Myrtle Avenue is shown with its width of 55 feet at both ends. The inset is bounded on the lower left by the heavy diagonal line against the main map and on the right by the heavy line against the Davey Co. inset.
notes: Placed from four building corners carried from sheet 44; rotation about -19 degrees agrees with the inset's north arrow.
Hinrich Place is Hinrichs Place today; Myrtle Avenue is Myrtle Street.

H. Davey Co paste-board mill on the Third River) not placed.

sheet-64.description: Sheet 64 is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north to the left. Molter Place and Clearfield Avenue lie along the top, north of the D.L.&W. Montclair Branch, which crosses the sheet from side to side. Watsessing Avenue runs down the left edge and Dodd Street runs diagonally from the upper left to the middle, with Lawrence Street and Harlow Street crossing the lower half. The principal works are those of H. B. Wiggins Sons Co., makers of woven wall coverings, in the upper right: a long printing, filling and drying building with boiler house, laboratory, rolling and drying rooms and a storage tank, described in a long text of fire precautions. A coal shed and several small buildings stand along the railroad on the left. The Watsessing M. E. Church and its Sunday school stand on Lawrence Street, and two rows of dwellings and flats line Lawrence Street. The Erie Railroad Orange Branch runs up the right side, and the dashed line labelled City of East Orange crosses the lower part.
notes: Placed from one hand-picked junction at Dodd, Orange and Watsessing with scale and north from the config; low confidence.
The modern Dodd Street and Lawrence Street node lies about 10 m from the drawn junction.
50 ft, north left. Molter Pl, Clearfield Av, Watsessing Av, Dodd, Lawrence; detector found nothing; anchored on Dodd/Orange/Watsessing (low).

sheet-65-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 65 is the main map, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the left. Arlington Avenue crosses the top diagonally, with the V. Nolls dairy farm and a few farm buildings south of it. The D.L.&W. Montclair Branch crosses the middle and the Erie Railroad Orange Branch runs up the left side. South of the railroad stands the large works of the Sprague Electric Co., with a long main building marked as mutual risk and admission refused, two long wings, a boiler house and several storehouses drawn in pink and yellow. Lawrence Street enters at the lower left and the dashed City of East Orange line crosses the lower part. A scale bar and compass rose are at the foot. An inset at the lower right shows the L. C. Harrison Co. organ works.
notes: Placed from carried hydrants and street corners at Lawrence Street, taken from sheet 64; low confidence.
The drawn Sprague Electric Co. appears as the Sawyer Mann Electric Co. plant on sheet 63.

50 ft. Two parts: 1 main (Arlington Av, Lawrence, Sprague Electric Co, Montclair Branch, Erie Orange Branch), anchored on corners carried from sheet 64 (low); 2 inset lower right (L. C. Harrison Co pipe organs on Orange / Hill), carried from sheet 61.

sheet-65-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 65 is an inset at the lower right, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned about 28 degrees from the neighbouring sheets, showing the works of the L. C. Harrison Co., makers of pipe organs, on the east side of Orange Street at its junction with Hill Street. The factory is a long building with an erecting room at the north end, an organ manufacturing room with voicing and metal piping on the first and second floors, a 25 horse-power engine, a wall-bearing section, a brick chimney and a machine shop at the south end. The text beside it notes one night watchman, fuel coal, lights electric and gas, fire killer tubes, city water and a 600 gallon water tank. Orange Street runs along the left edge and Hill Street across the foot, with hydrants and water pipes marked. The ground is the same as sheet 61 draws at 100 feet.
notes: Placed from five building corners carried from sheet 61; fitted scale 8.06 px/ft.

50 ft. Two parts: 1 main (Arlington Av, Lawrence, Sprague Electric Co, Montclair Branch, Erie Orange Branch), anchored on corners carried from sheet 64 (low); 2 inset lower right (L. C. Harrison Co pipe organs on Orange / Hill), carried from sheet 61.

sheet-66.description: Sheet 66 is drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north to the upper left. Bloomfield Avenue crosses the top corner and Grove Street runs down the right side. Brookside Place leaves Bloomfield Avenue at the top and runs south between two blocks of long narrow lots, with a few dwellings and a flats building on them and the nearest buildings of Frank Moorman, contractor, beside a brook. A small stream flows south through the middle of the sheet and a further tract is crossed by the Erie Railroad Orange Branch and the D.L.&W. Montclair Branch, which run diagonally across the lower left. Arlington Avenue lies at the lower left. The rest of the sheet is unbuilt land, and the line marked Town of East Orange crosses the foot.
notes: Brookside Place is probably La France Avenue today; placed from Bloomfield Avenue and Grove Street, low confidence.
100 ft. Bloomfield Av, Grove St, Brookside Pl (probably La France Avenue), Arlington Av; two points (low).

sheet-67-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 67 is the left side of the sheet, drawn at 200 feet to an inch with north toward the top, and covers the southern tip of Bloomfield where it meets the City of Newark and the City of East Orange. Watsessing Avenue runs down the left edge from Franklin Street at the top, meeting Grove Street, which continues south across Bloomfield Avenue to the bottom of the sheet. Bloomfield Avenue crosses the middle of the part from the west toward the southeast; north of it, small blocks of Thomas Street, Edison Street and Alva Street are outlined and marked 67, meaning that they are drawn in detail on the right-hand part of the same sheet, and Belmont Avenue appears at the dividing line. The Erie R. R. Orange Branch crosses the upper part diagonally. Most of the part is open land: the property of Thomas A. Edison north of Bloomfield Avenue, the John M. Dodd Estate on both sides of Grove Street, and the Orange Water Co. land with a reservoir in the south, crossed by a brook and the First River. The dash-dot line of the City of Newark runs along the heavy dividing line, and the City of East Orange line along the bottom. Only a few scattered dwellings are drawn, mostly along Watsessing Avenue. Adjoining sheets are numbered in the margins: 58 and 60 at the top left, 62 and 66 to the west. A pencil note in the top margin (Sept 1916) refers to an additional sheet.
notes: Thomas Street is today's Columbus Street.
Drawn at 200 ft to an inch; the right-hand part of the sheet (part 2) is at 50 ft.

sheet-67-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 67 is the right side of the sheet, beyond the heavy diagonal line, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned slightly from north. It shows the residential blocks at the southern end of Bloomfield along Bloomfield Avenue next to the Newark city line. Alva Street crosses the upper part, Thomas Street and Edison Street run down from it to Bloomfield Avenue, which crosses the lower part diagonally, and Belmont Avenue runs along the lower right edge, where the Belleville Township line is lettered. A brook crosses the blocks between Thomas and Edison Streets. The blocks are cut into narrow house lots with frame dwellings, several two-family houses, a bakery with its oven, a few stores near Edison Street and Bloomfield Avenue, tenements, and a public school near Belmont Avenue at the bottom right; the upper blocks north of Alva Street are mostly vacant lots. The City of Newark line runs along the heavy dividing line, which carries a See note for the sheet. Street widths of 50 and 60 feet are marked. The scale bar is drawn near the bottom right.
notes: Thomas Street is today's Columbus Street.
Fit from four junctions with residuals of 2 to 6 m; low to medium confidence.
